Subject: Third-party claim notice — urgent

Jordan / Kimberly,

Sorry to reach out on short notice. We received a formal claim notice yesterday from a third party asserting that a binary distributed by one of our upstream vendors (component: fastparser-xml) infringes their patent. Acme has asked Redwood to preserve evidence and confirm whether Redwood-supplied artifacts incorporate the same component.

Attached is the claim notice (ClaimNotice-Acme-20270329.pdf) and a log from our build system pointing to the supplier package. We need a clear statement from Redwood about whether the affected component is present in the deployed bundle for Acme, and whether Redwood will defend/reimburse per the MSA/order form. This is time-sensitive — Acme has a 10-business-day preservation window for evidence collection.

Please confirm next steps and let me know who at Redwood will be handling the legal coordination.

Thanks,
Rebecca
Rebecca Liu

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 8:14 AM Rebecca Liu <rebecca.liu@acme-industries.com> wrote:
> Jordan / Kimberly,
>
> Sorry to reach out on short notice. We received a formal claim notice yesterday from a third party asserting that a binary distributed by one of our upstream vendors (component: fastparser-xml) infringes their patent.

Thanks Rebecca — I’ve reviewed the claim packet attached. Quick summary from legal: the notice alleges asserted patent US 10,123,456 and identifies a binary signature that appears to match the vendor-supplied module. We need to confirm two things from our side:

1) Whether the module in question (fastparser-xml v1.2.3) is embedded in the version of the model-serving container that Redwood delivered to Acme (order form DL-8372, runtime image tag rwd/serve:20270301).
2) Whether Redwood’s MSA/order form indemnity obligations are triggered for third-party IP claims tied to vendor components used in customer deployments.

Immediate requests from us to Acme to support triage (Rebecca):
- Please confirm the file hashes from the claim notice and any sample files.
- Share the build-log lines that reference the component (we have the build-log-20270328.txt you attached — thx).

Internal proposed steps:
- Ops: snapshot the exact runtime image used by Acme and preserve the tarball in forensics bucket (do not delete).
- Engineering: run sha256 against the runtime image layers and compare to claim file hashes.
- Legal: analyze MSA indemnity language and prepare a proposed position (defend & indemnify, defend-only, or deny) and proposed redline for the order form (we should avoid broadness around vendor third-party dependencies).

Preliminary read: Redwood’s standard MSA includes a third-party IP indemnity limited to Redwood’s modifications and does not automatically cover upstream vendor claims unless Redwood directly incorporated the vendor binary as part of our deliverable. However, our Order Form has a customer-favorable schedule that could be read to broaden coverage for this account. I’ll prepare a concise memo and a redline proposal by tomorrow EOD.

I recommend we preserve communications with the vendor (Timothy CC’d) but route legal discussions through counsel channels.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Third-party claim notice — urgent (proposed redline & evidence request)

Rebecca / Jordan / Ben — final update and proposed next steps from Redwood legal: 

Summary (short):
- Engineering confirms the runtime image tag rwd/serve:20270301 includes a layer that matches the SHA256 in the claim notice. We have preserved the image tarball and build artifacts in the forensics bucket.
- Redwood’s standard MSA indemnity covers third-party IP only to the extent the claim arises from Redwood’s original code or modifications. The Order Form for DL-8372 contains language that could be read expansively; we propose a narrowly tailored approach to avoid setting a broad precedent.

Proposed customer-facing redline (high level):
1) Clarify that Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer only for third-party claims alleging infringement arising from (i) Redwood-originated code or (ii) third-party code specifically packaged and distributed by Redwood as part of a Redwood-branded deliverable (explicitly exclude upstream vendor binaries that are separately licensed to Customer unless Redwood expressly packaged them on behalf of Customer).
2) Add a cooperation & preservation clause that sets a 21-calendar-day evidence preservation window and requires prompt written notice and access to relevant artifacts.
3) Add an insurance offset clause: Redwood’s indemnity obligations will be reduced by any recoveries payable under applicable insurance policies (Redwood will pursue coverage where reasonable).

Evidence & timing request to Acme:
- Please provide the exact filenames and the sample binary you shared via secure link (we received sample-file.bin).
- We need access to the runtime image digest used by Acme (or permission to pull the same tag) and a list of endpoints where the image is deployed.
- Target timeline: Redwood will produce a short legal position memo and draft redline within 48 hours of receiving the full sample set and image access.

Commercial note to Ben/Jordan: if Acme objects to the narrowing redline we should be prepared to offer a limited credit (one-time service credit) or short-term indemnity limited to the current claim only. I’ll coordinate with finance on potential exposure estimates and with Ops on mitigation ETA.

If everyone agrees, I’ll send the proposed redline to Rebecca’s counsel and request a tight ESI/preservation protocol to meet Acme’s timelines. Approve to proceed?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
